paragraphs: Friend, this whole list is a reminder that a strong kingdom is built by many people, not one. The passage says these chiefs, "together with all Israel, bolstered and strengthened his kingdom, according to the word of the LORD concerning Israel" (1 Chronicles 11:10). Jashobeam, Eleazar, Abishai, Benaiah and a long roll call of names each had a part. I think God likes it when we show up with the part we've got, and it adds up to something big.

The most important moment is the water from Bethlehem. The Three risked their lives to bring it, and David poured it out to the LORD, saying, "How can I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives?" (1 Chronicles 11:18-19). He treated their sacrifice as something holy, not something to guzzle. And when the LORD brought about a great victory in the barley field (1 Chronicles 11:14), the win was credited to Him, not to the swords. Strong people matter, friend, but the LORD is the One who gives the victory.

So what does this mean for you at the oven today? Your part counts, even if it's a small one that nobody sees, and even if your name is way down the list. Honor the people who give up something for you, and give God the credit for what He does through you. Now go bake like it matters, because it DOES, and I'll be over here still screaming at the cookie sheet.
